summary: Gives recommendations to makers of home and small-office routers about the simple security features they should offer at the edge of an IPv6 network. It is informational and describes a baseline, not a full firewall design.

eli5.summary: A home router is like the front door of a house. This lists the basic locks the door should come with when the house uses the newer kind of internet addresses.

subtitle: Fifty recommendations for the basic packet filtering a home or small-office IPv6 router should do by default.

tldr.problem: Home IPv6 routers need some default protection like the one users got from IPv4 NAT, but a filter that is too strict breaks legitimate applications and one that is too loose leaves the home network exposed.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists numbered recommendations (REC-1 to REC-50): stateless filters for bad packets, then stateful filtering that only lets traffic in when an interior host started the flow, with minimum idle timers and rules for ICMPv6, UDP, TCP, SCTP, DCCP, IPsec and mobility.
tldr.outcome: It is informational, not a standard, and the IETF makes no claim that these filters improve security. Gateways must offer an easy transparent mode that turns the simple security off.

today: RFC 6092 is an Informational RFC from January 2011. It is not a standard, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Goals and Scope
sections.content:
This document gives recommendations for makers of residential and small-office IPv6 gateways, building on the "simple security" idea in RFC 4864. The gateways it describes are default routers for one local network and have one Internet-facing interface at a time. Only the packet filters between the interior network and the exterior networks are in scope.

The goals are to check traffic for basic sanity (spoofed or "Martian" packets), to require filter state to be opened by traffic that starts inside, to allow manually configured exceptions, and to isolate local DHCPv6 and DNS resolver services from the public Internet.

The RFC explains that IPv4 NAT set user expectations of stateful filtering that persist with IPv6. It also states plainly that conformance is not required to claim conformance with IETF IPv6 standards, and that the normative keywords are used only for precision. It adds the word DEFAULT, meaning the vendor-applied configuration before the administrator changes it.
sections.eli5: The router should keep out strangers and fakes, let in answers to things people at home asked for, and keep its own helpers private.

sections.title: Stateless Filters (REC-1 to REC-9)
sections.content:
Some packets must never be forwarded in either direction, whatever the network state.

  • Packets with a multicast source address (REC-1).
  • Multicast destinations at or narrower than the configured scope boundary, which SHOULD default to organization-local scope (REC-2).
  • Addresses forbidden on the public Internet, including deprecated site-local addresses and several reserved blocks (REC-3).
  • Packets with routing header type 0, which MUST NOT be forwarded; other deprecated extension headers SHOULD NOT be (REC-4).
  • Outbound packets whose source has no configured interior prefix, and inbound packets whose source claims to be an interior address, which stops spoofing (REC-5, REC-6).

By default, unique local addresses SHOULD NOT cross to or from the exterior (REC-7), inbound DNS queries MUST NOT reach an integrated resolver (REC-8), and inbound DHCPv6 discovery MUST NOT reach an integrated DHCPv6 server or relay (REC-9).
sections.eli5: Some letters are clearly fake or addressed to nowhere real, so the doorman throws them away no matter what. He also keeps the house's private helpers away from outsiders.

sections.title: Stateful Filtering for UDP, TCP, SCTP and DCCP
sections.content:
Transport traffic is not forwarded inward unless an interior endpoint solicited it, for example by matching the reverse path of earlier outbound traffic, or unless an administrator configured an exception. A filter keeps a state record per flow and deletes it after an idle timer.

The RFC borrows the terms of RFC 4787. With endpoint-independent filtering the exterior address is not checked when matching a packet to a flow; with address-dependent filtering it must match. Filters SHOULD be endpoint independent by default in gateways provisioned without service-provider management, favoring application transparency (REC-11, REC-17, REC-33).

For TCP, all valid packet sequences MUST be forwarded, including the 3-way handshake and simultaneous open (REC-31). An unsolicited inbound SYN gets an ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable code 1 response only after waiting at least 6 seconds, so simultaneous open is not broken (REC-34). SCTP follows the same pattern with INIT chunks (REC-38, REC-39), and DCCP is handled in a similar way (REC-43).

Whenever a gateway forwards a flow, it MUST also forward the matching ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable and Packet Too Big messages, and no ICMPv6 message may terminate a flow's state. The Packet Too Big case matters because path MTU discovery depends on it.
sections.eli5: The doorman writes down every call someone inside makes, and only lets in replies that match his notes. He waits a few seconds before telling a stranger to go away, in case a friend is calling back at the same moment.

sections.title: Idle Timers
sections.content:
Filters could be attacked by exhausting their state memory, so they must discard idle state, but not too soon. The RFC sets minimums so that live flows are not dropped.

  • Generic upper-layer protocols: not less than two minutes, default five minutes (REC-12).
  • UDP flows with both ports outside 0 to 1023: not less than two minutes, default five minutes (REC-14). Flows using well-known ports MAY expire sooner (REC-15).
  • TCP and SCTP established flows: not less than two hours four minutes, and transitory phases not less than four minutes (REC-35, REC-40).
  • DCCP open flows: not less than two hours four minutes, and transitory phases not less than eight minutes (REC-44).

A UDP state record MUST be refreshed by outbound packets and MAY be refreshed by inbound ones. The RFC warns that inbound refresh lets an attacker keep a record alive and, over many ports, use up state memory (REC-16).
sections.eli5: The doorman may forget an old call, but not too fast, because a quiet conversation can still be going on.

sections.title: IPsec, Mobility and Passive Listeners
sections.content:
Because IPsec secures traffic by definition, the default mode MUST NOT block Authentication Header, ESP, or UDP port 500 used by IKE (REC-21, REC-22, REC-24), and HIP extension headers must pass too (REC-26). ESP state SHOULD be indexed by interior address, exterior address and protocol, not by SPI (REC-25).

IPv6 mobility is meant to work: valid Mobility Header sequences MUST be forwarded for outbound and permitted inbound flows (REC-28), though unsolicited inbound Mobility Header messages from exterior mobile nodes are filtered unless covered by an IPsec policy. Shim6 packets must be forwarded for outbound and permitted flows (REC-47).

Applications that want inbound traffic without knowing peer addresses, which IPv4 NAT handled with NAT-PMP or UPnP-IGD, have no agreed IPv6 mechanism yet. Gateways SHOULD implement some protocol for this (REC-48) and MUST offer an easily selected transparent mode that forwards all unsolicited flows; that mode MAY be the default (REC-49). Subscriber-managed gateways MUST NOT offer management services to the exterior by default (REC-50).

The RFC says to take extra care with factory defaults, since most devices are never changed from them and their owners have no Internet engineering expertise.
sections.eli5: People with proper secret handshakes are let in, and there must be a big, easy switch to open the door fully. The control panel stays locked to outsiders.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC is frank that stateful filters create the illusion of a security barrier without the managed intent of a firewall. As noted in RFC 2993, the true impact of such tools may be a reduction in security. A perimeter model also assumes threats come from outside, which may leave interior hosts exposed to interior attack.

The filtering may be redundant when every IPv6 host runs its own host firewall, and the RFC says the vast majority of commercially available operating systems with IPv6 support had one at the time of writing. Allowing inbound IPsec and IKE can enable the unauthenticated mode of IPsec described in RFC 5386, which departs from IPv4 NAT expectations.

The gateway itself is also a target for denial-of-service attacks such as ping or SYN floods and should use the same protections as Internet application servers. The IETF makes no statement on whether using these capabilities improves security for any user.
sections.eli5: A doorman helps, but he is not a magic shield. Each person inside should also lock their own door.
